operations.title: Intrinsic primes generate a formal determinant Euler product
operations.statement: In the completed multiplicative monoid algebra of the conditional initial semiring, each intrinsic prime p has rank-one identity-inertia determinant L_p=(1-[p])^(-1)=sum_r[p^r). Unique factorization gives the coefficientwise identity product_p L_p=sum_(a nonzero)[a]. The analytic character [a] maps to a^(-s) for Re(s)>1 and recovers the classical zeta Euler product, but the character, continuation, completion, and zero spectrum are not Carrier-derived.
operations.scope: Conditional pointed-pi_0 formal Euler theorem; no full-Carrier lift, physical authorization, analytic continuation, or spectral zeros.

operations.title: Coefficientwise unique-factorization Euler test
operations.procedure: For each nonzero semiring element a, compute the coefficient of [a] in the product over intrinsic primes of sum_r[p^r]. Compare it with the coefficient in sum_a[a].
operations.expected_result: Existence and uniqueness of prime factorization make every coefficient exactly one. Any zero or multiplicity greater than one falsifies the theorem.
